mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains >4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the trigger period, or FEDFUNDS does not sustain the level for two months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly PAYEMS (employment) coincides with stronger consumer demand (HOUST), amplifying corporate hiring and investment, which drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS grows >2% month-over-month while HOUST rises >3% month-over-month
regime_hint: expanding labor market with rising demand
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return over 60 days when both proxies show the described pattern.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) below 100 suggests supply-side weakness, which predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or indistinguishable from baseline during INDPRO contraction.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4% for three consecutive months, lower labor cost pressures encourage corporate expansion, resulting in positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return during the UNRATE suppression period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% for 10 months indicates disinflation, which reduces risk premia and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or flat despite CPIAUCSL below 2% for the period.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both PAYEMS and RSAFS (retail sales) suggests robust consumer and business demand, which predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: expanding demand across labor and retail sectors
failure_condition: No significant positive return when both proxies show the described co-movement.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in GDPC1 (GDP) growth below -1% for two consecutive quarters signals a demand-driven recession, which is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or unchanged during the negative GDP growth period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for four consecutive months in a non-recession regime, lower policy rates reduce borrowing costs and boost equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% for four consecutive months and macro regime is not recessionary
regime_hint: low policy rate environment outside recession
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite FEDFUNDS below 2% for the required period.
